en: Although many mistakenly place it in Luzon, Mount Apo is actually the highest mountain located in the Mindanao island group.
While often incorrectly called the largest, Lake Lanao is actually the second largest lake, with Laguna de Bay being the true largest.
Despite common assumptions, Manila is not the largest city by land area; that title belongs to Davao City in Mindanao.
Many mistakenly believe Cebu is the largest island, but Luzon is actually the largest island in the Philippine archipelago.
Contrary to popular belief, the Pasig River does not flow from the sea to the lake, but rather from Laguna de Bay to Manila Bay.
Although often thought to be a single province, the Cordillera Administrative Region is actually composed of six distinct provinces in Luzon.
Despite its name sounding southern, the Sierra Madre mountain range is actually located along the eastern coast of Luzon, not Mindanao.
Unlike the misconception that the country has very few, the Philippines actually has 24 officially recognized active volcanoes, including Mayon and Taal.
Although some mistakenly think it lies south of the equator, the entire Philippine archipelago is geographically located in the Northern Hemisphere.
Despite its northern location near the Ilocos region, the island province of Batanes is officially part of the Cagayan Valley region.
Many incorrectly group it with the Visayas, but the island province of Palawan is officially part of the Mimaropa region in Luzon.
Contrary to the belief that Mount Mayon is in the Visayas, it is actually located in Albay province on the Luzon island group.
